rows.n: LUCUA Characters World — Pokémon Center Osaka & Nintendo OSAKA
rows.w: Osaka's answer to Tokyo's Character Street: LUCUA SOUTH opened 5 April 2026 and gathered Pokémon Center Osaka, Nintendo OSAKA and the ONE PIECE Mugiwara Store (moved from Daimaru Umeda) on its top floors, growing to 30+ character shops (Sanrio, Square Enix, Minecraft) by autumn 2026.
Kiddy Land's Kansai flagship (renewed April 2017 with Hankyu Sanbangai): character-specialist corners (Snoopy, Rilakkuma, Miffy and more), nekomart and toy/fancy goods.

Bandai's capsule-toy hall — about 1,000 gashapon machines, opened Dec 2020 as the chain's first Kansai store and billed as the region's largest; since March 2023 it trades inside Bandai Namco Cross Store Osaka Umeda, beside the HEP FIVE Ferris wheel.

Capcom's third store and first Kansai café (opened Nov 2022) — ~900 Monster Hunter / Resident Evil / Street Fighter goods plus a 56-seat rotating collab café; still trading in 2026 (Ōkami 20th-anniversary collab, June 2026) after the building's 13F became LUCUA SOUTH.
Six floors of manga, anime, retro games, idol merch, cosplay and collectibles, vintage to new; Mandarake's Osaka flagship relocated from Amerikamura to Den Den Town in December 2020.

rows.n: Pokémon Center Osaka DX & Pokémon Café
rows.w: Western Japan's only permanent Pokémon Café (opened 20 Sept 2019 with the DX store): Pikachu curry, Eevee pancakes and Pokéball desserts, reservation-only; reopened June 2026 after a renewal.

rows.n: Shinsaibashi PARCO Character Floors (Chiikawa Land · Donguri Republic)
rows.w: Shinsaibashi PARCO's 'POP CULTURE SHINSAIBASHI' floors gather character flagships with photo spots — Chiikawa Land (creator Nagano's official shop, 6F), a large Donguri Republic Ghibli store, Kiddy Land and more; directly linked to Shinsaibashi Station.
Osaka's Akihabara: electronics, anime, games and maid cafés along Sakaisuji in Nipponbashi.
One of western Japan's largest official anime/manga goods stores, the Ota Road anchor; the same building holds Lashinbang, Melonbooks and card-game floors.
Weekly Shōnen Jump's official shop (One Piece, Dragon Ball, Demon Slayer, Jujutsu Kaisen merch) on Daimaru Shinsaibashi's 9th-floor pop-culture zone beside Pokémon Center Osaka DX.

The third permanent Kirby Café (opened 21 Nov 2024) with Osaka-only dishes — a Waddle Dee okonomiyaki burger, kushikatsu in an Inhaling Kirby bowl, takoyaki-style petit cakes; reservations sell out months ahead.

rows.n: Kotobukiya Nipponbashi (コトブキヤ日本橋)
rows.w: Green-signed flagship of the plastic-model and figure maker: Ghibli, Nintendo, Square Enix and Marvel/Star Wars goods on 1F, current anime/game figures and modelling tools on 2F; in OSAKA-INFO's Nipponbashi pop-culture guide and OsakaMania's figure-shop series.

rows.n: Umeda Sky Building — Kuchū Teien Floating Garden Observatory
rows.w: The 173 m twin-tower skyscraper (1993) joined at the top by the open-air Floating Garden observation deck — 360° views over Osaka, open till 22:30.

One Michelin star (2026); second-generation fugu chef in Kitashinchi, wife a certified sake advisor — Osaka is one of Japan's biggest fugu-eating cities.
Michelin Two Stars (2026) Japanese restaurant; chef-owner Masamitsu Hisano sources the finest seasonal produce from across Japan.
Michelin Two Stars (2026) Japanese restaurant in Tenjimbashi.
One MICHELIN Star contemporary restaurant; Agu pork and Awaji lettuce from the chef's parents' farm, served shabu-shabu style, is one of the inspectors' favourite dishes.

A moss-covered Fudō Myōō statue that worshippers splash with water, beside two 80 m stone-paved alleys of old kappo counters, bars and okonomiyaki shops — the setting of Oda Sakunosuke's 'Meoto Zenzai'.
Western-style restaurant founded 1922 where omurice was invented in 1925; the main shop occupies a former tea house with tatami rooms and a garden in Nishi-Shinsaibashi.
"Osaka's Kitchen": a several-hundred-metre covered arcade of fishmongers, butchers, greengrocers and grill-it-on-the-spot stalls.

rows: 19 places · what Osaka is known for

rows.w: Michelin Bib Gourmand (2026) in Kitashinchi: creative kushiage that incorporates culinary influences from many countries — the sheer variety is endlessly fun.
Michelin Bib Gourmand (2023 guide) kushiage restaurant with uniquely inspired deep-fried skewer set menus.
Michelin Bib Gourmand (2026): stylish, bar-like Kitashinchi teppanyaki on polished iron and copper griddles — okonomiyaki standards through creative tonpeiyaki, with Italian wines.
Michelin Guide-listed kushiage counter whose chef focuses on seafood in his kushikatsu prix fixe, frying tiger prawn rare to draw out its sweetness.
Michelin Guide-listed Kitashinchi kushiage that works extravagant ingredients such as foie gras, truffles and caviar into its skewers.

Old-school Sennichimae okonomiyaki house cooking to order; its signboard dish is the suji negiyaki, beef strips and negi in a fluffy batter. Named by Time Out Osaka and Inside Osaka among Namba's okonomiyaki standbys and profiled by Savor Japan.

Dōtonbori okonomiyaki institution run across three generations, with a near-permanent queue; known for its yamaimo-yaki made with a mountain-yam batter (including a vegetarian, gluten-free version) (Inside Osaka; GLT/JTB Publishing).

Near-seventy-year-old okonomiyaki specialist by the Dōtonbori arcade, known for a cabbage-heavy, light batter; order the Ajinoya Mix (pork, squid, octopus, shrimp) or the negiyaki (Inside Osaka; GLT/JTB Publishing).

rows.n: Okonomiyaki Yukari Sennichimae (ゆかり 千日前店)
rows.w: Sennichimae branch of the Osaka okonomiyaki house credited with handing down the 'mixed' Osaka style; recommended in OSAKA-INFO's Japan Konamon Association konamon guide and in SAVOR JAPAN's 15 best okonomiyaki in Osaka.

rows.n: Hōzenji Yokochō Yakizen (法善寺横丁 やき然)
rows.nat: 法善寺横丁 やき然
rows.w: Okonomiyaki counter inside the stone-paved Hōzenji Yokochō alley; Rurubu's spot page highlights its blended flour, secret sauce and Hōzenji-yaki, and Mapple lists it among Minami's 17 okonomiyaki picks for its fluffy batter and suji negiyaki.

rows.n: Okonomiyaki Okaru (お好み焼 おかる, Sennichimae)
rows.nat: お好み焼 おかる, Sennichimae
rows.w: Shōwa-era Sennichimae okonomiyaki house of some 70 years, famous for the okami drawing Tsūtenkaku, Billiken or celebrities in mayonnaise on each pancake; in Rurubu's 12 must-eat okonomiyaki shops (Minami) and Kansai Walker's 8 popular okonomiyaki for visitors.

rows.n: Okonomiyaki Sanpei Shinsaibashi (おこのみやき 三平, Shinsaibashi-suji)
rows.nat: おこのみやき 三平, Shinsaibashi-suji
rows.w: Negiyaki specialist near Shinsaibashi known for its very tall green-onion pancakes; in Rurubu's 12 must-eat okonomiyaki shops (Minami) and Mapple's Minami/Kita okonomiyaki 17. (Separate shop from the Hōzenji Sanpei in the yokochō.)

Neo-Renaissance red-brick hall completed 1918 with a donation from stockbroker Einosuke Iwamoto (design Tatsuno Kingo & Okada Shin'ichirō); restored 1999–2002 and designated an Important Cultural Property in 2002. Free basement history exhibit.

1,300-year-old Umeda shrine named for Sugawara no Michizane's dew-and-tears poem; nicknamed after Ohatsu, heroine of Chikamatsu's 1703 'Love Suicides at Sonezaki', set in its grove — now a matchmaking power spot.
Claimed as Japan's longest covered shopping street — 2.6 km of shops and eateries running north from the Tenmangū approach.
A pocket of pre-war row houses east of Umeda whose narrow lanes are now full of cafés, craft shops and vintage stores.
The Umekita redevelopment beside JR Osaka Station — a large urban park with new towers opening in stages through spring 2027, next to the Grand Front Osaka complex.

The city art museum that opened on Nakanoshima in February 2022 — modern and contemporary art and design, part of the island's museum cluster.
The national mint where Japan's coins are struck; famous for opening its riverside avenue of cherry trees to the public each spring.
Contemporary Japanese and international art on two underground floors of Nakanoshima; the 2007 building's entrance structure is designed to evoke growing bamboo.
Osaka's grown-up entertainment quarter just south of Osaka Station — hundreds of restaurants, hostess bars and counters.

rows.n: Osaka Museum of Housing and Living (大阪くらしの今昔館)
rows.w: Walk-through, life-size reconstruction of an Edo-period Osaka merchant townscape on the upper floors of a building at the north end of Tenjinbashi-suji. Closed for renovation until 5 January 2027 (japan-guide e4024) — check before visiting.

Hands-on science museum and planetarium on Nakanoshima, next to the National Museum of Art.

The only museum anywhere with a permanent display of Kamigata (Osaka-Kyoto) ukiyo-e — realistic kabuki-actor prints of stars like Nakamura Utaemon III, ~30 works over four small floors, plus print-making classes (reservation). Free with the Osaka Amazing Pass.
Hideyoshi's 1583 castle, rebuilt in 1931 — the main keep (a museum with a top-floor lookout) rises from stone walls and moats in a vast park famous for plum and cherry blossom.

Jon Jerde's 2003 mall on the old Osaka Stadium site, shaped like a canyon of rock strata, with ~70,000 plants on its terraced rooftop Parks Garden.
Opened 2001 in a tower beside NHK Osaka, across from the castle: large-scale models chronicle the city from its days as Japan's first capital to the early Shōwa era, with views over the castle park.
The 'New World' district built after the 1903 Expo — half Paris, half Coney Island — around Tsūtenkaku, the 103 m tower rebuilt in 1956; the home of Osaka kushikatsu.
Osaka's city zoo (1915) in Tennōji Park, below Tsūtenkaku.

rows.n: Osaka City Museum of Fine Arts
rows.w: The 1936 municipal art museum in Tennōji Park, with Keitakuen garden behind it.

26 m mound in Tennōji Park long held to be a 5th-century kofun; it was Tokugawa Ieyasu's HQ in the Winter Siege and Sanada Yukimura's in the Summer Siege of Osaka (1614–15). Summit markers explain the battle.

rows.n: Kiyomizu-dera, Osaka (清水寺, Tamade no Taki)
rows.w: Osaka's own Kiyomizu-dera, with a mini 'Kiyomizu stage' looking toward Tsūtenkaku and the Tamade-no-taki waterfall — the only natural waterfall inside Osaka city; listed by Time Out Osaka and Osaka Metro's Osaka Mania (Kiyomizu-zaka).

rows: 2 places · kept for the record, newest check first

rows.w: CLOSED: Dōtonbori's neo-Renaissance theatre (opened 1923 as a cinema, kabuki/stage house since 1997) gave its final performance, the 'Onagori Gogatsu Ōkabuki', on 26 May 2026 after 103 years; Shochiku plans to demolish the ageing building. Facade-only now — no shows.

1956 Sennichimae leisure building whose 2nd-floor warren of tiny bars and the Misono Universe hall made it an Ura-Namba nightlife legend; tenants left at the end of 2024 and the whole building closed on 5 July 2025 ahead of redevelopment.
